title: 30/60/90 remediation roadmap (Google Doc)
description:
Earlier directive from Amaka, now under review: 'The board will not authorise an eighteen-month transformation. They will authorise the first ninety days. Show me the ninety days that earn the rest.'

**Submission via Google Doc link.** A 30/60/90 is a table; tables don't render in the pad. Create a Google Doc, set sharing to **'Anyone with the link → Viewer'**, paste the URL below with a 60+ word abstract.

**Required structure — one table:**

| # | Window (30 / 60 / 90 days from board-approval) | Action (concrete, verb-first) | Owner role | Budget tier (S < ₦5M / M ₦5–25M / L ₦25M+) | Dependency or blocker | Acceptance criterion | Stage 1–3 evidence cite | NIST CSF 2.0 function/category | ISO 27001:2022 Annex A control |

**Required rows (in this order — 9 mandatory, 3 per window):**

**Days 0–30 (containment + immediate hardening):**
  1. Rotate every credential and IAM role token that touched the breached workstation (cite Stage 3 task 1).
  2. Apply egress-network policy that blocks server-initiated traffic to RFC 1918 link-local + abuse-block IP ranges by default (cite Stage 2 task 6).
  3. Deploy file integrity monitoring on `~/.bashrc` and `/etc/sudoers.d/*` across all production workstations (cite Stage 3 tasks 2 & 3).

**Days 31–60 (detection + audit):**
  4. Automated weekly audit of all `/etc/sudoers.d/*` entries with diff alerting (cite Stage 3 task 3).
  5. Deploy EDR rule for T1546.004 and T1548.003 indicators (cite Stage 3 task 6).
  6. Mandatory IMDSv2 enforcement across every EC2 instance, by AWS account (cite Stage 2 task 6).

**Days 61–90 (governance + structural):**
  7. Parameterised-query lint gate added to CI pipeline; rejecting concatenated SQL on PR (cite Stage 2 task 3).
  8. JWT verification audit across every service: explicit algorithm allow-list, no `alg:none` accepted (cite Stage 1 task 7).
  9. GDPR breach-notification runbook table-top exercise with Legal + DPO (cite Stage 4 task 2).

**You must add one more row for interim security leadership and privileged-access separation after the Amaka allegation.** You may add up to 2 additional rows of your own choosing. (Maximum 12 rows.)

**Citation bar:**
- Every action cites at least one Stage 1–3 artefact (task number + the file/log line/payload).
- Every action names one dependency/blocker and one acceptance criterion that an auditor could verify.
- Every action maps to one NIST CSF 2.0 function/category (visit https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework for the canonical 2.0 taxonomy — `GV` function exists since Feb 2024).
- Every action maps to one ISO 27001:2022 Annex A control by ID (e.g. `A.5.15 Access control`, `A.8.7 Protection against malware`, `A.8.16 Monitoring activities`). Made-up Annex A IDs lose 4 pts each.

**Quality bar:**
- Concrete actions only. 'Improve security culture' loses 5 pts. 'Run a mandatory secure-coding training for all backend developers in days 60–75, ≥80% attendance gates Q3 performance reviews' passes.
- Budget tiers are realistic — none of these actions are budget-tier S except #1 (staff hours, no procurement).
- Each window has a milestone the board can name back to you.

**One mistake I almost made (in the Doc, 60+ words):** a specific moment you nearly mis-sequenced — e.g. putting EDR rule deployment (window 30–60) before credential rotation (window 0–30) because EDR is technically more interesting, and the harm that ordering would have caused (the attacker still has a valid IAM token while you instrument detection).

**Minimum 650 words in the Doc** (table + window commentary). Paste link + 60+ word abstract below.

**Audit findings response (mandatory, 90+ words):** Use `06-external-audit-findings.md` and `08-front-page-amaka.md`. For each audit finding, state whether your roadmap accepts, disputes, or defers it, and cite the row number that implements the response or the deferral-list item that explains why it waits. Include one sentence on why the interim-security-leadership row is not optional.

**Explicit deferral list (mandatory section, 100+ words in the Doc).** After the 30/60/90 table, name **at least three real items from Stages 1-3 that you are deliberately NOT scheduling inside this 90-day window**, and why each one waits. For each:\n  • Name the weakness (cite Stage X task Y).\n  • State the deferral target window (days 91-180 / 181-365 / "tracked only").\n  • Justify in one sentence WHY this one waits — capacity, dependency on an earlier control, lower blast-radius, or compensating control already in place.\n\nGeneric "nothing deferred" loses 15 pts. The board judges discipline by what you say no to, not what you say yes to. A roadmap with no deferrals is a wish list.

---

**Universal grading rule.** Generic answers fail. Every claim in your submission must be tied to specific evidence — an artefact from the lab (file path, log line, command output, payload, screenshot) **and** at least one external citation where research is relevant (NIST section number, MITRE technique ID, CVE, vendor advisory, ISO control ID, GDPR article). Claims without an attached artefact, timestamp, payload, standard section, or business constraint earn zero for that claim. Lab-only answers earn partial credit. External-only answers earn partial credit. Full credit requires both.
